excerpt: Maven is a platform for live, cohort-based online courses taught by working experts in AI, product, leadership, design, engineering and business. Founded by Udemy and altMBA veterans; backed by a16z and First Round.
content:
Maven hosts live online courses taught by practitioners rather than academics. Instead of pre-recorded video you watch alone, a Maven course runs over a few weeks with a group of students (a cohort) who meet live with the instructor, do projects and learn from each other. Its website describes live courses with real-world experts in AI, product, leadership, design, data and engineering, marketing and sales, and business and finance, plus free short Lightning Lessons. For instructors, Maven provides an all-in-one platform including course landing pages, and its teach page says experts keep about 90% of their revenue.

Maven was founded by Gagan Biyani, a co-founder of Udemy; Wes Kao, a co-founder of altMBA; and Shreyans Bhansali, who previously started Socratic, according to Andreessen Horowitz's investment announcement. TechCrunch reported in May 2021 that Maven raised a $20 million Series A led by a16z, seven months after emerging from stealth with a $4.3 million round led by First Round Capital and three months after a $750,000 equity crowdfunding round. a16z partner Andrew Chen joined the board.

Maven changed direction in 2022. TechCrunch reported that September that it would focus less on courses from online creators with big audiences and more on courses taught by star employees and operators from tech companies, after finding that a large following did not guarantee a successful course. TechCrunch put Maven's known funding at about $25 million, from investors including a16z, First Round Capital, Naval Ravikant, Sahil Lavingia, Li Jin and Arlan Hamilton.

For students, each course has its own price set by the instructor, shown on its landing page; Lightning Lessons are free. For teachers, Maven takes a share of course revenue rather than a subscription. This profile draws on Maven's own pages and published reporting. We have not taken a Maven course, and nothing here is paid placement.
